claims.text: Replacing EAM reference potentials with DNN interatomic potentials trained on ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch for multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
The proposed reference potential will be trained on a wide array of atomic configurations obtained from ab initio simulations of the liquid.
DNN potentials can be used to describe both solid and liquid states of high-entropy materials near melting.
The intervention is applicable above approximately 3000 K for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is applicable to near-equiatomic high-entropy-alloy compositions.
A comprehensively trained DNN more accurately reproduces liquid local atomic arrangements than EAM.
A comprehensively trained DNN more accurately reproduces liquid pair correlations than EAM.
EAM has a limited ability to represent the relevant liquid configurations.
DNN potentials capture many-body and subtle interatomic effects that are absent from EAM formulations.
Capturing these additional interatomic effects improves overlap between the DNN reference and ab initio liquid configuration spaces.
Enhanced configuration-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path length and mismatch.
The DNN reference may yield approximately an order-of-magnitude reduction in thermodynamic-integration mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy estimates.
TOR-TILD uses EAM reference potentials for traditional thermodynamic integration.
The improvement may be confined to high-temperature refractory or similar high-entropy-alloy systems and may not transfer to lower-melting or differently bonded materials.
